data.narrative:
RobCo is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Roman Hölzl, Paul Maroldt, and Constantin Dresel, having raised $160M+ to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—spanning robotics and manufacturing, including firms like Humanoid, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Generalist AI at adjacent stages (Seed through Series B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $160M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $320M. Peer-median analysis examines five same-sector comparables at same or adjacent stage, producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The five-company peer sample includes two Series B companies valued at $2.0B and $1.8B, one Series B at $1.6B, one Series A at $1.4B, and one Seed-stage company at $1.1B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $272M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $985M across the two methods. The substantial spread reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation positioning within the peer set. Key variables include RobCo's specific technical differentiation relative to the Series B cohort and trajectory assumptions embedded in peer multiples, neither of which can be resolved from available data alone.
